summary.headline: Triveni Turbine Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3% YoY to ₹4.91bn and PAT dropped 41.7% to ₹533mn, while record order booking hit ₹7.64bn (+17.2%).
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹4.91bn, down 3% YoY, as domestic sales rose 51.8% to ₹3.4bn but exports fell 46.6% to ₹1.51bn. EBITDA margin compressed to 17.5% (vs 26.3% a year earlier) and PAT margin to 10.4%, which management attributed to domestic/export mix, product/aftermarket mix and a loss-making NTPC order. Order booking hit a company record of ₹7.64bn, led by exports (+49%) and product orders (+32.5%), and the closing order book rose 10.5% to ₹24.53bn. Management guided to a sharp margin reversion in H2, with Q4 stronger than Q3, but said FY27 profit growth over FY26 would not be significant.

financial_highlights.change: -46.6% YoY; export share 30% vs 55% in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Product (domestic + export)
segments.commentary: Product order booking grew 32.5% to ₹6.01bn in Q2. Domestic order booking was down 2.5% to ₹3.79bn (H1 down 16%), with market share lower in steel while the market grew.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 aftermarket order booking fell 17.8% and was 21% of orders. H1 aftermarket orders rose 12.3% to ₹13.33bn (29% share), and the closing aftermarket order book more than doubled to ₹6.39bn (26% of book vs 14% a year ago). Q2 aftermarket revenue fell 16.7% to ₹1.48bn.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 export order booking grew 49% to 48% of quarterly orders (38% a year ago). H1 export orders rose 51.6% to ₹7.5bn (56% share). Export revenue in H1 fell 24%, with deferred shipments to Middle East customers expected in Q3/Q4.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 margins to revert upward on product mix and export/aftermarket contribution; Q4 expected to be stronger than Q3.
Remaining ~15% of NTPC order billing to be spread equally across Q3 and Q4; NTPC losses already provided for, with possible future claims treated as upside.
FY27 profitability expected to grow over FY26 but not significantly; consolidated PBT margin roughly consistent with last year per management.
H2 FY27 revenue growth indicated at around 25%+ (management's indication on questioner's question).
Management expects order booking growth in Q3 and FY28 visibility to support growth; FY28 described as providing greater growth avenue.
No data center order expected to be lumpy; Q2 booking described as regular, not including large one-offs.
capex_capacity: US gas turbine refurbishment/parts contract via South African subsidiary, with a European partner: potential ₹ equivalent of USD 80-90mn over 4-5 years, with only in-year portion booked annually.
Gas turbine product development (for non-power applications) and small gas turbines planned as multi-year R&D programs; no timelines given beyond 'short' development frames for services.
Advanced platforms with significantly better cost structure to be rolled out, expected to positively affect margins in coming quarters.
Combined cycle steam turbine order for US data center-linked application: 2 x 25 MW steam turbine added to pre-existing gas turbine (about 150 MW combined cycle plant).
demand_pricing: Domestic inquiry book flat vs Q1; US inquiry visibility up substantially (data center, combined cycle, energy storage, carbon capture); Central/South America plateauing; Southeast Asia, Europe and India flat.
Management says competition with largest global steam turbine maker (with Indian operations) is unchanged; pricing in India much lower than global markets.
Export pricing lucrative, with margins significantly higher than domestic.
Middle East enquiries expected to rise as war-related disruption eases; drive turbine enquiries from EPCs expected to finalise in Q4.
Aftermarket cycles: spares 3-4 months, servicing about a quarter, refurbishment 5-12 months (complex projects 3-4 quarters); about 80% of opening order book typically executed in the year.
Commodity price increases pushed up material costs in Q1, expected to normalise by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why are domestic order inflows lower in H1 FY27 versus last year, and which sectors are lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market grew, led by steel, but Triveni's share fell, and domestic booking in Q2 roughly doubled from Q1 as cement and steel order finalisation had been delayed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and timeline of the gas turbine refurbishment contract and the small gas turbine plans?
qa_highlights.answer: The potential is USD 80-90mn over 4-5 years, through a South African subsidiary with a European partner. The gas turbine product is a multi-year effort aimed at non-power applications.

qa_highlights.question: Were the NTPC order losses already accounted for, and can H2 margins exceed 18-19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NTPC losses are already provided for, with possible claims later. It said H2 margins should be significantly healthier, but gave no specific percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record ₹7-8bn quarterly order booking a sustainable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 had no lumpy large orders and that booking responds to market demand, with commodity price increases lifting values; it declined to set a steady-state figure.

qa_highlights.question: How does aftermarket order-to-revenue conversion work, given that order inflows have outpaced revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Refurbishment takes 3-4 quarters for complex projects, while spares and servicing are mostly in-year. Management declined to give a full breakup but said 80% of opening order book usually executes in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US data center combined cycle order a repeat of an expected first data-center order, and how is the US pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q2 order was a combined cycle steam turbine add-on to a gas turbine, with the end user a data center. It said less than 5% of the inquiry book is combined cycle.

risks_watch: Margins: EBITDA margin of 17.5% and PAT margin of 10.4% in Q2; management's H2 reversion depends on export and aftermarket mix and on Q4 execution.
Domestic market share loss in steel and larger-turbine segments versus the global competitor, with domestic orders down 16% in H1.
NTPC BFW/energy storage order (about 15% of value still to bill) executed at low or negative margins, with a commissioning requirement in Q4.
Middle East and export deferrals tied to freight/transport issues and regional war disruption; H1 export revenue down 24%.
Working-capital intensity rising if Triveni moves toward solution/EPC-style scope, which management flagged as a strategic option.
Tax refunds not yet accounted for, which could be a P&L upside later.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident about order momentum and H2 recovery but candid that Q2 was disappointing on margins and growth. Answers were detailed on the refurbishment and export pipeline but vague on NTPC order economics, FY27 profit growth and market share drivers.
key_quotes: Overall ladies and gentlemen Q2 has been disappointing but it was as expected from a margin and as well as growth perspective.
So we do anticipate a reversion to our mean, which would mean that the performance in Q3 and Q4 would be substantially better, Q4 more than Q3.

The product mix will obviously mean that the margins will be significantly healthier in H2 and when we look at it on a year-on-year basis between FY26 and FY27 we would anticipate a growth in profitability but it will not be significant.

adds.what: 2 x 25 MW steam turbine added to pre-existing ~150 MW combined cycle plant for US data-center-linked application (order, not company-owned capacity)

growth.why: Management cut FY27 growth to 'marginal' (profit growth over FY26 'not significant'), but guided H2 FY27 revenue growth around 25%+, backed by a record ₹7.64bn quarterly order booking and a ₹24.53bn closing order book (+10.5%) with no company-owned capacity additions disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 17.5% from 26.3% a year ago; management guided a sharp H2 reversion on product/aftermarket mix and export contribution, with Q4 stronger than Q3, though no percentage was given and the NTPC order is still a drag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No company-owned plant, line or capacity addition was disclosed; the only 'adds' are customer orders (2 x 25 MW steam turbines on an existing ~150 MW combined cycle plant).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 revenue growth of around 25%+, backed by a record ₹7.64bn quarterly booking (+17.2%) and a closing order book of ₹24.53bn (+10.5%), though H1 revenue was down and exports fell 24%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief gives no utilisation figure and no board plan for new investment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 profit growth was cut to 'marginal' and described as 'not significant', so the call points away from a guidance raise despite the H2 revenue indication of around 25%+.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 margin recovery depends on Q4 execution, NTPC billing (about 15% still to bill, with a Q4 commissioning requirement) and export deferrals to Middle East customers expected in Q3/Q4 after H1 export revenue fell 24%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gas turbine for non-power applications and small gas turbines are multi-year R&D programmes with no timelines beyond 'short' service frames, and advanced platforms with a lower cost structure will roll out, with no dates given.

rows.label: US gas turbine refurbishment contract via South African subsidiary
rows.why: Potential of USD 80-90mn over 4-5 years with a European partner, with only the in-year portion booked annually, so the timing and conversion are uncertain.

rows.label: US data-center and combined-cycle demand
rows.why: US inquiry visibility rose substantially (data center, combined cycle, energy storage, carbon capture) and the Q2 US combined-cycle order was booked, though less than 5% of the inquiry book is combined cycle.

rows.label: Export pricing and margin mix
rows.why: Export margins are described as significantly higher than domestic, and exports were 48% of Q2 orders and 59.2% of the closing order book, so mix should support H2 margins.

tone.note: Management was confident on order momentum (record ₹7.64bn booking) and H2 recovery, but candid that Q2 margins and growth disappointed and it was vague on NTPC economics, FY27 profit growth and domestic share loss; analysts pushed on margin levels and the sustainability of order run rates.
